newsitem.title: FRANCE: Framatome/GEC Alsthom merger plan fails - paper.
newsitem.headline: Framatome/GEC Alsthom merger plan fails - paper.

text.p: French state-controlled nuclear power plant builder Framatome has written off initial proposals from Franco-British venture GEC Alsthom for a merger, but is still open to talks, La Tribune newspaper said on Monday.
Le Tribune said the Framatome board had decided at a meeting on Friday that the talks on initial merger proposals had come to nothing and were now definitively abandoned.
Alcatel Alsthom Chairman Serge Tchuruk had already conceded in March that the talks with Framatome had run into difficulties but said the plan had not been abandoned.
The newspaper quoted a source close to the case as saying the latest Framatome board decision did not mean talks would come to an end with Alcatel and GEC.
"Nothing stops us from considering alternative scenarios," it quoted the source as saying.
It was not possible to get a comment immediately from Framatome.
The news comes just days after the French government said a bid by GEC for state-controlled defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF was ineligible for national security reasons.
GEC said in the wake of that announcement that it was talking to Alcatel and Lagardere, both French and allowed to bid for the state's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said over the weekend the government was prepared to look at offers for Thomson-CSF which included partnerships.
